newsitem.title: USA: Dow to buy Lilly stake in Dow Elanco for $900 million.
newsitem.headline: Dow to buy Lilly stake in Dow Elanco for $900 million.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said on Thursday it would acquire Eli Lilly and Co.'s 40 percent stake in their agricultural chemicals joint venture, Dow Elanco, for $900 million plus undistributed earnings.

The transaction, a result of Lilly's decision to exercise its option to sell its interest, will make Dow the sole owner of the Indianapolis-based operation, which was formed in 1989 and has annual sales of about $2 billion.

The venture combined the plant science businesses of both parent companies, as well as Dow's speciality pest management business. Since its formation, DowElanco has seen strong growth in sales and profits, Dow said.

"We view the agricultural products business as an engine for growth, which will be accelerated by Dow Elanco's increased commitment to agricultural biotechnology," William S. Stavropoulos, Dow's president and CEO, said in a statement.
"This acquisition is part of our value growth strategy to increase investment in performance businesses."
Dow, the world's fifth-largest chemical company, called Dow Elanco "one of the world's largest research-based agricultural companies."
The company develops, manufactures and markets products for management of weeds, insects and plant disease and for urban pest control.
Dow Elanco also is majority owner of Mycogen Corp., an agricultural biotechnology company that develops and markets technology-based seed and pest management products.
Dow Chemical also announced that it would repurchase an additional 20 million shares.
Dow Chemical's stock gained $1 to $89.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange while Lilly added 62.5 cents to $93.25, also on the NYSE.

Dow Chemical said the new stock buy-back will begin once the current repurchase authorisation is completed in the second quarter. The shares will be bought on the open market or in private transactions.
Since January 1995, Dow has repurchased 55.3 million shares, equivalent to about 20 percent of its outstanding stock. As of April 30, Dow had 231.9 million shares outstanding.
